en: Ever since that game, I've thought about when this day would come. I was determined to prove you betrayed me.
But I gradually stopped training. I couldn't fully commit when I didn't know where or how I'd find you.
When you beat me the first time, that lit a fire under my ass. So I could replicate Akamatsu's pitching for one final duel!
The stage is finally set. Think back, Shinada. Remember exactly how it was. The regional tournament final, twenty years ago.
Bottom of the ninth in a scoreless tie, two outs, runners on second and third. On the mound is Akamatsu, the tournament's top pitcher.
Get in the box, Shinada!
Well? What now, Shirakawa? You convinced yet?
Well? Are you?
...Yeah. There's no two ways about it. Not after that. Your batting's seriously something else.
But I think I knew that a long time ago. I just couldn't force myself to admit it.
When you, my former teammate, were accused of sign stealing... I thought you were a fraud.
A fake. A dirty cheat. A wannabe pro, grasping for fame he didn't deserve.
When I thought of you like that, it made sense why you took that wild swing.
You challenged Akamatsu just to earn more respect. And that selfishness robbed me of baseball!
...Those kinds of thoughts consumed me. My hatred of you kept growing. Snowballing.
But now I understand. You were the real thing, too. A true, professional player. Not the kind of guy who'd put himself before the team.
That homer you hit as a Wyvern⑬you really didn't cheat, did you?
Damn right I didn't. When it comes to baseball, I'm pure as a puppy. Not even a drop of guile in me.
Heh, I suppose that's one way to put it.
Heheh. Come on, man. Have some faith in your old teammate.
Faith... Now that's a word you don't hear much these days. But you know what? You're right.
I guess I didn't trust my teammates back then. Not really.
My left shoulder was shredded from overuse, but I never told anyone. Not the coach, and certainly not anyone from the team.
I wasn't thinking about the future at all. The only thing that mattered was Koshien, and earning our right to be there.
If I had stepped out of my shell and confided in someone, maybe my career would have gone differently.
...Actually, I knew about your shoulder. And that you were trying to hide it.
I never told anyone, though. Because I knew how you felt. If I had an injury, I would have kept it a secret too.
We all felt the same way. Back then, getting to Koshien was everything. No one thought about what might happen next.
I guess a batter like you would have noticed something was off with my throwing.
I get it now. I finally understand why you challenged Akamatsu.
If we went into extra innings with the score knotted, you were afraid my damaged shoulder would give out.
That's what made you take that swing. So I wouldn't have to pitch anymore.
Knowing full well you'd take the blame if you blew it.
...Honest to goodness, that's a little too far back for me. Can't remember what I was thinking.
Oh... No need to thank you then. Boy, am I glad I stopped myself in time.
Come on, what's with the attitude? It's not like a thank-you costs anything.
Heh, isn't it a bit late to drop the act?
...So, Shirakawa. What are you gonna do now?
I'm going back to Tokyo. I took all this time off, and the guys at the office are probably swamped with work.
You know, it feels like a huge weight's been lifted from my shoulders. For the first time, I can finally wake up in the morning with a renewed sense of purpose.
That's great to hear. You take care, okay?
Yeah. Sorry for being such an asshole, Shinada.
Oh, and one more thing!
Thanks!

Ahem! I was talking about restaurants.

Do you go to famous restaurants a lot, Shion-chan?
Yes, but I always make reservations beforehand, so I've never had the experience of waiting outside.
Smart thinking. If there's a line, you're stuck outside even if it rains. That sucks.
It's all the more important if you know the weather will be bad. I only go to restaurants with open-air seating if the forecast looks clear.
I used to check the weather before baseball games, but we have domed stadiums now. Now I just don't take an umbrella if it's clear when I leave.
Oh, that's not good. Buying an umbrella when you're out and about is expensive. Maybe you should bring a collapsible umbrella with you.
Wait, do you have an umbrella on you right now?
Of course! There was a thirty percent chance of rain today, so it made sense to bring one out with me.
Wow, that's amazing! Now I kind of wish it would rain so we could walk close under your umbrella together.
What was that last part?
Oh, uh, nothing!
Isn't that a pain? What if you want to go somewhere in the spur of the moment? Do you still call ahead?
But of course. How else am I supposed to know if there's open seating available?
But if you make a reservation, you have to get there at a set time, right? I don't like having my schedule locked down like that.
I think it's worse to not have a reservation and get stuck waiting outside.
But if it's for a fancy restaurant, isn't that kind of thing part of the experience? It's not special if you can just walk in and eat.
Oh, excuses, excuses. It would be better to skip the wait and use the time that's been freed up to do other things.
Yeah, I get it. I just feel that life is less fun if it's all planned out.
What if you can't reserve? Wouldn't you have to go without one then?
Oh, I don't go to restaurants like that. I can't patronize an establishment that doesn't provide reserved seating.
What if I were seated next to a really loud group? And the worst would be sharing a table with strangers.
But that's the best part! I've had a great time sitting around a table with strangers and watching a ball game on TV together.
And the people in Kineicho are all Wyverns fans, right? So that's always a great ice breaker.
Does that sort of thing actually happen?
Sure it does! I've met a ton of people like that here!

In Shinada's Side Story "The Cost of a Swing,"  Shinada's batting skills can be improved to give an advantage when taking on challengers.
Shinada's batting skills are improved by playing various courses at the batting center.

The bat's swing has four impact ranges that are assigned to four buttons: <Action:Button_Circle@Cost_Of_A_Swing>, <Action:Button_Triangle@Cost_Of_A_Swing>, <Action:Button_Square@Cost_Of_A_Swing> and<Action:Button_Cross@Cost_Of_A_Swing>. If an impact range levels up, its Swing Cursor is enlarged, making it easier to hit.
If the impact timing levels up, the window of opportunity for hitting a home run is extended.

If the fouling skill levels up, the window of opportunity for fouling off pitches is extended.
This is useful in situations where Shinada needs to cut pitches.
If Heat Eye levels up, pitches will appear even slower when using the Heat Eye ability.

If Batting Eye levels up, the pink circle that indicates the ball's anticipated trajectory becomes smaller, making it easier to hit. It also improves the precision of the anticipated pitch indicator at the screen's bottom right.
